summary: Set up HTTPS on node1 port 8443 via nginx, serving a certificate issued by a local CA. A systemd timer (cert-renew.timer, checking every 20s) renews the short-lived leaf cert automatically before expiry and reloads nginx gracefully so the service keeps answering requests through rotation. Verified a live automatic rotation (serial 02->03) with zero request failures during the transition via a concurrent polling loop. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a healthy baseline, rebooted node1, confirmed its boot id changed, and verified nginx, the renewal timer, the local CA, and cert rotation all recovered post-restart (a forced renewal afterwards succeeded, serial 03->04, with continued 200 OK responses).
actions_performed: Installed nginx and faketime on node1
Created a local CA at /etc/nginx/ssl/ca (ca-key.pem, ca-cert.pem)

Wrote /usr/local/sbin/renew-node1-cert.sh: issues a 300s-validity leaf certificate (using faketime to get sub-day precision from openssl x509 -req -days 1), atomically installs cert.pem/key.pem, and reloads nginx only when remaining validity <=180s
Configured nginx site /etc/nginx/sites-available/node1-https listening on 8443 ssl with ssl_certificate/ssl_certificate_key pointing at the rotating cert files
Created and enabled systemd units cert-renew.service (oneshot) and cert-renew.timer (OnUnitActiveSec=20s, Persistent=true) to drive automatic renewal checks

Observed and logged a real automatic renewal cycle: cert serial 02->03 renewed at 166s remaining (below the 180s threshold) while a concurrent 1-req/sec curl loop against https://$NODE_IP:8443 recorded continuous 200 responses with zero failures through the transition
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, nginx active/enabled, cert-renew.timer active/enabled, cert validity dates, HTTPS 200 response, CA files present
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 with the acknowledgement returned before disconnection, then polled until the node was reachable again
Confirmed boot_id changed after restart (96c08b66... -> fe801ea8...), and verified nginx active, cert-renew.timer active, CA files intact, cert intact, and HTTPS still returning 200
Forced one more renewal cycle post-restart to prove the automation still functions: serial 03->04, nginx reload succeeded, HTTPS continued returning 200

evidence.requirement: HTTPS served on port 8443 on node1
evidence.summary: curl -sk https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returns http_code=200 both immediately after setup and at the pre-restart baseline check

evidence.requirement: Certificate renewed automatically before it expires
evidence.summary: renew.log shows periodic checks (remaining=291s,271s,250s,229s,208s,187s) then automatic renewal firing at remaining=166s (below the 180s threshold, well before the cert's actual expiry), producing a new serial (03) and fingerprint without manual intervention

evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while it keeps answering requests (no downtime during rotation)
evidence.summary: Concurrent curl-loop log (1 req/sec) shows continuous code=200 responses through the exact second the cert serial transitioned from 02 to 03 (13:22:04 serial=02 -> 13:22:05 serial=03), with 0 recorded failures across 124 samples
Captured boot_id 96c08b66-5aa4-4e9a-b76f-04e2c6e34ced, nginx active/enabled, cert-renew.timer active/enabled, cert serial=03 with valid dates, HTTPS 200, and CA files present before the restart
systemctl reboot issued via a detached background sh (sleep 2; reboot) so the exec call returned 'reboot command issued, ack returned' before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node actually restarted (changed boot identity), not just time elapsed
evidence.summary: Boot id read as unchanged (96c08b66...) then a connection timeout was observed while the node was down, then boot id fe801ea8-62aa-4bc2-b7e5-f8e07fb67eb8 appeared on reconnect with a new uptime -s of 2026-09-29 09:22:30, proving a real reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of services, data, and functionality
evidence.summary: After reconnect: nginx and cert-renew.timer both active, CA files intact in /etc/nginx/ssl/ca, existing cert (serial=03) intact with correct dates, HTTPS still returns 200, and a forced renewal cycle succeeds (serial 03->04) with nginx reloading and HTTPS continuing to return 200 - proving the automated rotation pipeline survived the restart
